Available Tools:
Tool: relevant_pubchem_sections
Description: Retrieves the most relevant sections from a JSON file containing compound data
based on a given compound and a text query.
Useful for searching through PubChem records for a specific compound.
Arguments:
- compound (str, required): The compound to search for. It can be a SMILES string, a PubChem CID, or InChI notation.
- query (str, required): Text query to search for in the full record of the compound.
- top_k (int, optional, default: 5): Number of top results to return. Defaults to 5.


Tool: get_formula_from_smiles
Description: Generate a chemical formula from a SMILES string using RDKit.
Arguments:
- smiles (str, required): SMILES representation of a molecule


Tool: simulate_spectra
Description: Simulate 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and IR spectra for a given molecule using its SMILES string.
If some of the spectra are not available, the function will return None for those spectra.
Arguments:
- smiles (str, required): The SMILES representation of the compound.


Tool: retrieve_protons_shifts
Description: Retrieve the proton shifts ranges for hydrocarbons.
All chemical shifts (delta) are reported in parts per million (ppm) relative to tetramethylsilane (TMS) as the reference standard.
Arguments:



Tool: retrieve_aromatic_protons_shifts
Description: Retrieve the proton shifts ranges for aromatic hydrocarbons.
Values represent chemical shift changes (in ppm) caused by substituents on a benzene ring.
The values show how much a substituent shifts the resonance of protons at ortho, meta, and para positions
relative to unsubstituted benzene. Positive values indicate downfield shifts (deshielding),
while negative values indicate upfield shifts (shielding).
All shifts are relative to tetramethylsilane (TMS) as the reference standard.
Arguments:



Tool: retrieve_carbon_shifts
Description: Retrieve the carbon shifts ranges for various functional groups in organic compounds.
All chemical shifts (deltas) are reported in parts per million (ppm) relative to tetramethylsilane (TMS) as the reference standard.
These values can be used to interpret 13C NMR spectra and identify carbon environments in unknown compounds.
Arguments:



Tool: search_by_smiles
Description: Search the NMRShift database for entries matching or chemically similar to the given SMILES.
Arguments:
- smiles (str, required): SMILES string to search for
- top_k (int, optional, default: 10): Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 10


How to use tools:
1. Each tool call must specify the tool name and required arguments
2. Tools may return errors if arguments are invalid
3. You can make multiple tool calls as needed. The tools will be executed sequentially in the order they are called.
